transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I feel like people at work are secretly plotting against me, even when they tell me they’re not. It has gotten to the point where my husband and my manager at the restaurant strongly encouraged me to come see someone. I just can't shake the feeling that there's this plan to get me fired.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, especially when no one else is around?

Yes, I actually do. Especially at work and late at night, I'll hear my name being called or voices whispering that I'm screwing up and don't deserve my job. It happens even when I can clearly see there's nobody around me and the kitchen is quiet.
How long have these experiences—like hearing voices and feeling people are plotting against you—been happening?

These specific things—the whispering and the strong feeling that people are plotting against me—have been happening regularly for about four months now. It has gotten especially noticeable over this past busy season at the restaurant.
Have you ever had a period lasting more than a month where you felt completely back to your usual self, without any of these symptoms?

No, I haven't had any periods where I felt back to my usual self at all. Since the restaurant's ownership change over a year ago, it has just been a continuous, steady decline without any breaks. Things have only gotten more intense over the last four months since the voices and the feelings of plotting started.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F20", "F23"], but based on this conversation, F23 (acute and transient psychotic disorders) is unlikely because the symptoms have been continuously present for more than four months without any remission. The chronicity and lack of return to baseline rule out acute and transient psychosis, which by definition involves a time-limited course. In contrast, the persistent delusions (persecutory beliefs about coworkers plotting), auditory hallucinations (voices commenting on performance), and continuous decline over time strongly support a diagnosis within the schizophrenia spectrum (F20). Therefore, the current candidate is narrowed to F20.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent delusions (persecutory beliefs about coworkers and management plotting against her) and auditory hallucinations (hearing voices commenting on her performance) for at least four months, with no remission and continuous functional decline over the past year. These symptoms meet the ICD-10 criteria for schizophrenia (F20), particularly given the presence of core psychotic symptoms and duration. Delusional disorder (F22) is considered but less likely due to the presence of hallucinations and broader symptom profile beyond fixed delusions.
